nodes.name: Neighborhood system and graph
nodes.statement: Given sites $S=\{s_1,\ldots,s_N\}$, a neighborhood system is $\mathcal{G}=\{\mathcal{G}_s, s\in S\}$ with (1) $s\notin\mathcal{G}_s$ and (2) $s\in\mathcal{G}_r \iff r\in\mathcal{G}_s$. The pair $\{S,\mathcal{G}\}$ is a graph; a clique $C\subset S$ is a subset whose distinct sites are mutually neighbors.
nodes.statement_clean: A neighborhood system on a set of sites is a symmetric, irreflexive collection of neighbor sets; cliques are subsets of mutual neighbors.

nodes.name: Markov Random Field (MRF)
nodes.section: IV. Markov Random Fields and Gibbs Distributions
nodes.statement: A random field $X=\{X_s, s\in S\}$ on $\{S,\mathcal{G}\}$ is an MRF if $P(X=\omega)>0$ for all $\omega\in\Omega$ and $P(X_s=x_s\mid X_r=x_r, r\neq s) = P(X_s=x_s\mid X_r=x_r, r\in\mathcal{G}_s)$.
nodes.statement_clean: An MRF is a strictly positive random field whose conditional distribution at each site depends only on its neighbors.

nodes.name: Gibbs distribution
nodes.section: IV. Markov Random Fields and Gibbs Distributions
nodes.statement: A Gibbs distribution on $\Omega$ relative to $\{S,\mathcal{G}\}$ has the form $\pi(\omega)=\frac{1}{Z}e^{-U(\omega)/T}$, where $U(\omega)=\sum_{C\in\mathcal{C}} V_C(\omega)$ is the energy summed over cliques, $T$ is temperature, and $Z=\sum_\omega e^{-U(\omega)/T}$ is the partition function.
nodes.statement_clean: A Gibbs distribution is a normalized exponential of an energy summed over cliques, parameterized by temperature.

nodes.name: Potential
nodes.section: IV. Markov Random Fields and Gibbs Distributions
nodes.statement: A potential is a family $\{V_C, C\in\mathcal{C}\}$ of functions on $\Omega$ such that each $V_C(\omega)$ depends only on coordinates $x_s$ with $s\in C$.

nodes.name: Local characteristics
nodes.section: IV. Markov Random Fields and Gibbs Distributions
nodes.statement: The local characteristics of an MRF are the conditional probabilities $\pi(x_s\mid x_r, r\neq s)$. For a Gibbs distribution: $\pi(x_s\mid x_r,r\neq s)=Z_s^{-1}\exp(-T^{-1}\sum_{C:s\in C} V_C(\omega))$.

nodes.name: Image model $X=(F,L)$ with intensity and line processes
nodes.section: I. Introduction; III. Graphs and Neighborhoods
nodes.statement: The original image is the pair $X=(F,L)$ where $F=\{F_{i,j}\}_{(i,j)\in Z_m}$ is the intensity (gray-level) process on the lattice $Z_m=\{(i,j):1\le i,j\le m\}$ and $L=\{L_d\}_{d\in D_m}$ is a line (edge) process on the dual lattice $D_m$.
nodes.statement_clean: The image is modeled as a pair of a pixel-intensity field and a hidden line/edge field on the dual lattice.

nodes.name: Degraded image model
nodes.statement: The degraded image is $G=\varphi(H(F))\odot N$ where $H$ is a shift-invariant blur, $\varphi$ a memoryless (possibly nonlinear) sensor transformation, $N$ is independent Gaussian white noise with mean $\mu$ and variance $\sigma^2$, and $\odot$ is invertible (e.g. $+$ or $\times$).

nodes.name: Posterior energy $U^P$
nodes.statement: Given prior energy $U(f,l)$ and degradation $G=\varphi(H(F))\odot N$, the posterior energy is $U^P(f,l)=U(f,l)+\|\mu-\Phi(g,\varphi(H(f)))\|^2/(2\sigma^2)$, where $\Phi$ inverts $\odot$.

nodes.name: Annealing schedule
nodes.section: X. Stochastic Relaxation; XII. Gibbs Sampler: Mathematical Foundations
nodes.statement: An annealing schedule is a decreasing sequence $T(t)$ of temperatures used in successive site updates; it is admissible if $T(t)\to 0$ and $T(t)\ge N\Delta/\log t$ for all $t\ge t_0$, where $\Delta=U^*-U_*$.

nodes.name: Minimal energy configuration set $\Omega_0$
nodes.statement: $\Omega_0=\{\omega\in\Omega: U(\omega)=\min_\eta U(\eta)\}$, with $\pi_0$ the uniform distribution on $\Omega_0$.

nodes.name: MRF-Gibbs equivalence (Hammersley-Clifford)
nodes.section: IV. Markov Random Fields and Gibbs Distributions
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a neighborhood system. Then $X$ is an MRF with respect to $\mathcal{G}$ if and only if $\pi(\omega)=P(X=\omega)$ is a Gibbs distribution with respect to $\mathcal{G}$.
nodes.statement_clean: The Markov property on a graph is equivalent to having a Gibbs distribution whose energy decomposes over cliques.
conclusions: $X$ is an MRF $\iff$ $\pi$ is a Gibbs distribution with respect to $\mathcal{G}$

nodes.name: Posterior is Gibbsian
nodes.statement: For each $g$ fixed, $P(X=\cdot\mid G=g)$ is a Gibbs distribution over $\{S,\mathcal{G}^P\}$ with energy $U^P(f,l)=U(f,l)+\|\mu-\Phi(g,\varphi(H(f)))\|^2/(2\sigma^2)$, where $\mathcal{G}^P_s=\mathcal{G}_s$ for $s\in D_m$ and $\mathcal{G}^P_s=\mathcal{G}_s\cup\mathcal{H}^2_s\setminus\{s\}$ for $s\in Z_m$.
nodes.statement_clean: Under the degradation model, the posterior over the image given data is again a Gibbs distribution, with a slightly enlarged neighborhood determined by the blur kernel.
conclusions: $P(X=\cdot\mid G=g)$ is Gibbs with energy $U^P$ on $\{S,\mathcal{G}^P\}$

nodes.name: Proof of posterior-Gibbs theorem
nodes.statement: Apply Bayes' rule, use Gaussianity of $N$ to write $P(G=g\mid X=\omega)\propto e^{-\|\mu-\Phi(g,\varphi(H(f)))\|^2/(2\sigma^2)}$, and decompose terms by clique structure to identify the posterior neighborhood.

nodes.name: Theorem A (Relaxation / Convergence of Gibbs Sampler)
nodes.statement: Assume that for each $s\in S$ the visiting sequence $\{n_t, t\ge 1\}$ contains $s$ infinitely often. Then for every starting configuration $\eta\in\Omega$ and every $\omega\in\Omega$, $\lim_{t\to\infty} P(X(t)=\omega\mid X(0)=\eta)=\pi(\omega)$.
nodes.statement_clean: If every site is visited infinitely often, the Gibbs Sampler distribution converges to the target Gibbs distribution regardless of the initial state.
assumptions: $X$ is an MRF with Gibbs distribution $\pi(\omega)=e^{-U(\omega)/T}/Z$
Every site $s\in S$ appears infinitely often in the visiting sequence $\{n_t\}$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem A (Relaxation)
nodes.statement: Show the (nonstationary, irreducible, aperiodic) Markov chain has $\pi$ as its unique invariant measure and prove a contraction inequality (Lemma 1) on transition kernels over full sweeps; iterate the contraction to obtain convergence.

nodes.name: Express transition matrix and invariance
nodes.statement: Define the transition matrix $(M_t)_{\eta,\omega}=\pi(X_{n_t}=x_{n_t}\mid X_s=x_s, s\neq n_t)$ if $\eta=\omega^x$ for some $x$, else $0$. Verify $\pi M_t=\pi$ so $\pi$ is invariant.

nodes.name: Contraction lemma over full sweeps
nodes.statement: Lemma 1: there exists $0<r<1$ with $\sup_{\omega,\eta,\eta'}|P(X(t)=\omega\mid X(0)=\eta)-P(X(t)=\omega\mid X(0)=\eta')|\le r^{K(t)}$, where $K(t)$ counts completed sweeps. Proof uses lower bound $\delta=\inf \pi(x_s\mid x_r,r\neq s)>0$.

nodes.name: Conclude via invariance and contraction
nodes.statement: Using $\pi M_t=\pi$, write $|P(X(t)=\omega\mid X(0)=\eta)-\pi(\omega)|\le \sum_{\eta'} \pi(\eta')|P(X(t)=\omega\mid X(0)=\eta)-P(X(t)=\omega\mid X(0)=\eta')|\le r^{K(t)}\to 0$.

nodes.name: Theorem B (Annealing)
nodes.statement: Suppose there is $\tau\ge N$ with $S\subset\{n_{t+1},\ldots,n_{t+\tau}\}$ for every $t$. Let $T(t)$ be decreasing with $T(t)\to 0$ and $T(t)\ge N\Delta/\log t$ for all $t\ge t_0$, where $\Delta=U^*-U_*$. Then for any $\eta\in\Omega$ and every $\omega$, $\lim_{t\to\infty} P(X(t)=\omega\mid X(0)=\eta)=\pi_0(\omega)$, the uniform distribution on the minimal-energy set $\Omega_0$.
nodes.statement_clean: If the temperature is cooled at least as slowly as $N\Delta/\log t$ and every site is visited within every window of length $\tau$, the Gibbs Sampler converges to the uniform distribution on the minimum-energy configurations (the MAP set).
assumptions: There exists $\tau\ge N$ with $S\subset\{n_{t+1},\ldots,n_{t+\tau}\}$ for every $t$
$T(t)\ge N\Delta/\log t$ for all $t\ge t_0$, with $\Delta=U^*-U_*$
conclusions: $\lim_{t\to\infty} P(X(t)=\omega\mid X(0)=\eta)=\pi_0(\omega)$ for all $\omega,\eta$, where $\pi_0$ is uniform on $\Omega_0=\arg\min_\omega U(\omega)$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem B (Annealing)
nodes.statement: Combine two lemmas: Lemma 2 gives a uniform contraction for the time-inhomogeneous chain under the annealing schedule (using $\delta(t)\ge L^{-N}e^{-\Delta/T(t)}$ and $\sum (t_0+k\tau)^{-1}=\infty$); Lemma 3 shows $\|P_{t_0,t}-\pi_0\|\to 0$ via $\|\pi_T-\pi_0\|\to 0$ as $T\to 0$ and a triangle-inequality telescoping bound.

nodes.name: Lower bound on local characteristics under cooling
nodes.statement: Show $\delta(t)\ge L^{-N}e^{-\Delta/T(t)}$, hence $\inf P(X(T_k)=\omega\mid X(T_{k-1})=\omega')\ge CL^{-N}/(t_0+k\tau)$ when $T$ follows the schedule (Lemma 2).

nodes.name: Divergence-of-series gives forgetting
nodes.statement: Since $\sum_k 1/(t_0+k\tau)=\infty$, the product $\prod_{k=1}^m(1-c/(t_0+k\tau))\to 0$, so the chain forgets its initial condition (Lemma 2).

nodes.name: Convergence of $\pi_{T(t)}$ to $\pi_0$
nodes.statement: Verify $\pi_T(\omega)\to \pi_0(\omega)$ as $T\to 0$ and that $\sum_t\|\pi_{T(t)}-\pi_{T(t+1)}\|<\infty$ via monotonicity of $\pi_T(\omega)$ in $T$ for small $T$.

nodes.name: Telescoping triangle inequality
nodes.statement: Using $\|P_{t_0,t}-\pi_0\|\le \|P_{t_0,t_0}-\pi_{T(t_0)}\|+\sum_{k=t_0}^{t-1}\|\pi_{T(k)}-\pi_{T(k+1)}\|+\|\pi_{T(t)}-\pi_0\|$ and Lemmas 2-3, conclude $\|P_{t_0,t}-\pi_0\|\to 0$, hence Theorem B.

nodes.name: Theorem C (Ergodicity)
nodes.statement: Assume $\tau$ exists such that $S\subset\{n_{t+1},\ldots,n_{t+\tau}\}$ for all $t$. Then for every function $Y$ on $\Omega$ and every starting configuration $\eta\in\Omega$, $\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{n}\sum_{t=1}^n Y(X(t))=\sum_\omega Y(\omega)\pi(\omega)$ with probability one.
nodes.statement_clean: Time averages along the Gibbs Sampler converge almost surely to expectations under the Gibbs distribution.
assumptions: Every site $s\in S$ is visited within every $\tau$-window of the schedule

nodes.name: Gibbs Sampler
nodes.statement: Site-by-site stochastic relaxation that updates $X_{n_t}$ by drawing from its conditional distribution given the current values at all other sites; produces a Markov chain with equilibrium measure $\pi(\omega)=e^{-U(\omega)/T}/Z$.
input: Visiting sequence $\{n_t\}\subset S$ with each $s$ visited infinitely often
output: Sequence of configurations $X(1),X(2),\ldots$ converging in distribution to $\pi$

nodes.name: Initialize
nodes.statement: Choose any starting configuration $X(0)=\eta\in\Omega$ and set $t=0$.

nodes.name: Select next site
nodes.statement: At time $t$, take site $n_t\in S$ from a fixed visiting sequence (e.g. raster scan) such that every site appears infinitely often.

nodes.name: Sample from local characteristic
nodes.statement: Draw $x\in A_{n_t}$ from $\pi(X_{n_t}=x\mid X_s=X_s(t-1), s\neq n_t)=Z_{n_t}^{-1}\exp(-T^{-1}\sum_{C: n_t\in C} V_C(\omega^x))$, set $X_{n_t}(t)=x$ and $X_s(t)=X_s(t-1)$ for $s\neq n_t$.

nodes.name: Iterate (with optional cooling)
nodes.statement: Increment $t\to t+1$ and repeat. For MAP estimation, use temperature schedule $T(t)\ge N\Delta/\log t$ (annealing); for sampling at fixed temperature, keep $T$ constant.

nodes.name: Metropolis algorithm
nodes.statement: Given current state $X(t)$, propose $\eta$ at random, compute $\Delta\mathcal{E}=\mathcal{E}(\eta)-\mathcal{E}(X(t))$ and $q=e^{-\beta\Delta\mathcal{E}}$; accept the move with probability $\min(1,q)$, else stay.

nodes.name: Simulated annealing
nodes.statement: Use the Metropolis (or Gibbs Sampler) algorithm with a decreasing sequence of temperatures $\{T_n\}$ to drive the system toward minimum-energy ground states.

nodes.name: MAP image restoration
nodes.section: I. Introduction; IX. The Computational Problem
nodes.statement: Given degraded data $G=g$ and prior MRF $X=(F,L)$, find $\arg\max_{\omega} P(X=\omega\mid G=g)$, equivalently $\arg\min_{(f,l)} \big(U(f,l)+\|\mu-\Phi(g,\varphi(H(f)))\|^2/(2\sigma^2)\big)$.

nodes.name: Sampling from a Gibbs distribution
nodes.statement: Generate samples $\omega\sim\pi$ where $\pi(\omega)=e^{-U(\omega)/T}/Z$ on a high-dimensional configuration space $\Omega=\prod_s A_s$.

nodes.name: Computing expectations under a Gibbs distribution
nodes.statement: Compute $\mathbb{E}_\pi[Y]=\sum_\omega Y(\omega)\pi(\omega)$ for functions $Y$ on $\Omega$ when direct evaluation of $Z$ is intractable.

nodes.name: Ising model energy
nodes.section: IV. Markov Random Fields and Gibbs Distributions
nodes.statement: $U(\omega)=\alpha\sum_{i,j} x_{i,j}+\beta\big(\sum_{i,j} x_{i,j}x_{i+1,j}+\sum_{i,j} x_{i,j}x_{i,j+1}\big)$, the binary, homogeneous, isotropic case of pairwise nearest-neighbor potentials.

nodes.name: Logarithmic annealing schedule (used in experiments)
nodes.statement: $T(k)=C/\log(1+k)$, where $k$ is the number of full sweeps; $C$ chosen large enough to satisfy $T(k)\ge N\Delta/\log k$ in theory, but small (e.g. $C=3.0$ or $4.0$) in practice.

nodes.name: MRF restoration on 5-level images
nodes.statement: Original image is a sample of an MRF on $Z_{128}$ with $L=5$ intensities and 8-neighbor system; pairwise potentials $V_C(f)=-\beta$ if $f_s=f_r$ and $+\beta$ otherwise. Restorations from additive Gaussian noise ($\sigma=1.5$) and from blur+nonlinearity+multiplicative noise are produced via the Gibbs Sampler with annealing.

nodes.name: Hand-drawn image with line process
nodes.statement: $64\times 64$ image with three gray levels degraded by Gaussian noise; restoration with and without an explicit line process $L$ on the dual lattice, using cliques of size four for $U(l)$. Adding the line process yields markedly cleaner edges.

nodes.name: Boundary finding on roadside scene
nodes.statement: $64\times 64$ blurred and noised roadside photograph (~0 dB) with a line process supporting four directions per site; energies for size-4 line cliques chosen by rotation-invariant rules. After 1000 iterations the algorithm produces a continuous boundary delineating sign and arrow.

nodes.name: Parallelism of the Gibbs Sampler
nodes.statement: Because each site update uses only its neighbors, the Gibbs Sampler can be implemented in parallel: assign one processor per site or partition $S$ into independently updated regions; refresh time grows only with neighborhood size, not $N$.

nodes.name: Hierarchy expands the marginal graph
nodes.section: IV. Markov Random Fields and Gibbs Distributions (closing remark)
nodes.statement: Marginalizing the joint MRF $(F,L)$ over the line process $L$ yields a marginal distribution on the intensities $F$ whose graph is fully connected, so a hierarchical model with local cliques can encode long-range interactions.

nodes.name: Logarithmic cooling rate is too slow in practice
nodes.statement: The bound $T(t)\ge N\Delta/\log t$ in Theorem B is impractical (e.g. $N=20000, \Delta=1$ requires $e^{40000}$ visits to reach $T=0.5$); experiments use $T(k)=C/\log(1+k)$ with small $C$ over a few hundred sweeps and obtain good restorations.
